There are many orders in the scriptures for the depiction of the form of God. These forms are not material. If God is omnipresent, He must also exist in material elements. There is no doubt about this matter. But atheists think the opposite. Although they preach that every
thing is God, but when they go to the temple and see the form of God, then they
refuse to consider it as God. According to their own principle, every thing is God, then why is this
archa-vigraha not God? In reality, they have no idea about God. But the sight of devotees
is different from these, their sight remains filled with love for God. Upon seeing God in his various forms,
they become filled with love, because, unlike atheists, they do not see any difference between God in the temple and God. In the temple, the pleasant face of Shri Vigraha appears divine and
spiritual to the devotees, and the adornment of God's body seems extremely dear to the devotees.
It is the duty of the Guru to decorate the Shrivigraha in the temple, to clean the temple, and to tell the method of worshiping the Shrivigraha. In Vishnu temples, many rituals are followed.

Seeing the smiling and attractive form of God, and hearing his very enchanting
words, the pure devotee loses all his other consciousness. His senses
become free from all other functions and become absorbed in devotion. Thus, unwillingly,
he spontaneously becomes HUTS. Note: There are three classes of devotees--the superior, the middle, and the inferior. Devotees up to the lowest class
become liberated. This verse states that even without knowledge, by seeing the decoration of the idol in the temple, the devotee, absorbed in its meditation, loses all other consciousness.
In this way, by stabilizing oneself in Krishna consciousness and engaging the senses in the service of God,
man unknowingly becomes liberated. This is also confirmed in the Bhagavad Gita. Only
by performing unmixed devotion approved by the Shakhas, a man becomes equal to Brahma. It is said in the Bhagavad Gita:
Brahmabhooyaya Kalpate. This means that the soul is Brahman in its original state,
because it is a part of the Supreme Brahman. But by forgetting this true nature of oneself, that one is an eternal servant of God, one becomes deluded by Maya. The forgetfulness of one's true natural
state is Maya. Otherwise, it is eternally Brahman. When a person is taught to be aware of their situation, then understanding
seems that he is a servant of God.
'Brahma' is the sign of the state of self-realization. Here,
even the lowest-ranking devotee who does not have the knowledge of the ultimate truth and who only
devoutly bows to God, contemplates on him, sees him in the temple,
and brings flowers and fruits to offer in the idol, he too, unknowingly, becomes liberated. Devotees: That is, with utmost devotion, the devotees respect the idol and

even a low-class devotee is in a divine state compared to them, who try to attain liberation through contemplation or other means. Even those who are non-dualists like Shukdev Goswami and the four Kumaras
became devotees, fascinated by the beauty of the idols in the temple, by the fragrance of the Tulsi offered to God.
Although they were in a liberated state, instead of remaining non-dualists, they became devotees, fascinated by the beauty of God. Here, the word 'Vilas' is noteworthy. From 'Kilaas' comes the manifestation of the activities or divine plays of God.
In the functions of temple worship, it is certain that a person should not go to the temple to see God
only decorated, but he should listen to the reading of Shrimad Bhagavat Bhagavad Gita or such
literature, whose regular recitation takes place in the temple. In Vrindavan, this is the custom
that in every temple, the scriptures are recited. Even the lowly devotees,
who have neither literary knowledge nor the leisure to read the Bhagavata or the Bhagavad Gita,
get the opportunity to listen to the divine plays of God. In this way, their minds
are constantly immersed in the thoughts of God--in their forms, actions, and their divine nature.
